Runtime provider probe — reads `provider-probe.json` and returns the best\n//! provider for each NOAA model (GFS, HRRR, NBM, …).\n//!\n//! The probe file is written by `xtask probe-providers`. At runtime, callers\n//! call [`ProviderProbe::load`] to read the cached results.  The file has a\n//! 24-hour TTL by default; callers can re-run `xtask probe-probes` to\n//! refresh it when it becomes stale.\n//!\n//! # Re-probe triggers\n//!\n//! Providers should be re-probed in three cases:\n//! 1. **File absent**: `ProviderProbe::load` returns `Err`\n//! 2. **File stale**: `is_fresh()` returns `false` (timestamp > 24h old)\n//! 3. **Consecutive HTTP errors**: `ProviderFailureTracker::should_reprobe()` returns `true`\n//!\n//! The `ProviderFailureTracker` from `gribtract_fetch` tracks consecutive\n//! HTTP failures per provider at runtime. Use it alongside the staleness check:\n//!\n//! # Example\n//!\n//! This example shows the complete runtime provider selection workflow with\n//! re-probe triggers for staleness and consecutive HTTP errors:\n//!\n//! ```no_run\n//! use gribtract::ProviderProbe;\n//! use gribtract_fetch::probe::ProviderFailureTracker;\n//! use std::path::Path;\n//!\n//! // Load provider probe results\n//! let probe = match ProviderProbe::load(Path::new(\"provider-probe.json\")) {\n//!     Ok(p) => p,\n//!     Err(_) => {\n//!         // Case 1: File absent — trigger re-probe\n//!         eprintln!(\"provider-probe.json not found, running initial probe...\");\n//!         run_probe_and_write_json(); // Your implementation\n//!         return;\n//!     }\n//! };\n//!\n//! // Initialize failure tracker (threshold = 3 consecutive errors)\n//! let tracker = ProviderFailureTracker::default_threshold();\n//!\n//! // Check if we should re-probe (Case 2 OR Case 3)\n//! // is_valid() checks both: file staleness AND consecutive failures\n//! if !probe.is_valid(24 * 3600, &tracker) {\n//!     // Get specific providers that need re-probing for logging\n//!     let needing = probe.providers_needing_reprobe(&tracker);\n//!\n//!     if !probe.is_fresh(24 * 3600) {\n//!         eprintln!(\"provider-probe.json is stale (>24h old), triggering re-probe...\");\n//!     }\n//!\n//!     if !needing.is_empty() {\n//!         eprintln!(\"Re-probe triggered by consecutive failures: {}\",\n//!             needing.join(\", \"));\n//!     }\n//!\n//!     run_probe_and_write_json(); // Your implementation\n//!     return;\n//! }\n//!\n//! // Safe to use cached provider rankings\n//! if let Some(provider) = probe.best_provider(\"gfs\") {\n//!     println!(\"Best GFS provider: {provider}\");\n//!\n//!     // After HTTP requests, record success/failure\n//!     match fetch_data_from_provider(provider).await {\n//! .as_secs();\n                now.saturating_sub(probe_secs) < max_age_secs\n            })\n            .unwrap_or(false)\n    }\n\n    /// Iterate over all probe results.\n    pub fn results(&self) ///\n    /// let probe = ProviderProbe::load(Path::new(\"provider-probe.json\")).unwrap();\n    /// let tracker = ProviderFailureTracker::default_threshold();\n    ///\n    /// // Check if probe is \"provider-probe\")]\n    pub fn is_valid(&self, max_age_secs: u64, tracker: &gribtract_fetch::probe::ProviderFailureTracker) -> bool {\n        // First check staleness\n        if !self.is_fresh(max_age_secs) {\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        // Then check if any tracked provider has exceeded the failure threshold\n        for (_model, providers) in &self.rankings {\n            for provider in providers {\n                if tracker.should_reprobe(provider) {\n                    return false;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        true\n    }\n\n    /// Get providers that need re-probing due to consecutive failures.\n    ///\n    /// Returns a list of provider names that have exceeded the consecutive failure threshold.\n    /// This can be used to log which providers are problematic before triggering a re-probe.\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    /// * `tracker` - The `ProviderFailureTracker` from `gribtract_fetch`\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    /// A vector of provider names that need re-probing\n    #[cfg(feature = \"provider-probe\")]\n    pub fn providers_needing_reprobe(\n        &self,\n        tracker: let min: i64 = time_it.next()?.parse().ok()?;\n    let sec: i64 = time_it.next()?.trim_end_matches('Z').parse().ok()?;\n\n    // Days since 1970-01-01 via Hinnant's algorithm (inverse of civil_date).\n    let days_since_epoch = ymd_to_days(year, month as u32, day as u32)?;\n    let total_secs = days_since_epoch * 86400 + hour * 3600 + min * 60 + sec;\n    if total_secs < 0 {\n        return None;\n    }\n    Some(total_secs as u64)\n}\n\n/// Proleptic Gregorian (year, month, day) → days since 1970-01-01.\n/// Returns `None` for obviously invalid inputs.\nfn ymd_to_days(y: i64, m: u32, d: u32) -> Option<i64> {\n    if !(1..=12).contains(&m) || !(1..=31).contains(&d) {\n        return None;\n    }\n    // Hinnant civil_from_days inverse:\n    // shift year so March = month 0\n    let (y, m) = if m <= 2 { (y - 1, m + 9) } else { (y, m - 3) };\n    let era = if y >= 0 { y } else { y - 399 } / 400;\n    let yoe = y - era * 400; // [0, 399]\n    let doy = (153 * m as i64 + 2) / 5 + d as i64 - 1; // [0, 365]\n    let doe = yoe * 365 + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100 + doy; // [0, 146096]\n    Some(era * 146_097 + doe - 719_468)\n}\n\n// ── Tests This ensures tests that check\n    /// staleness with a 24-hour threshold will always see this as fresh.\n    fn fresh_timestamp() -> String {\n        let now = std::time::SystemTime::now()\n            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)\n            .unwrap_or_default()\n            .as_secs();\n\n        // Go back 1 hour to ensure we're well within the 24-hour threshold\n        let one_hour_ago = now.saturating_sub(3600);\n\n        // Convert Unix seconds back to ISO-8601\n        // This is the inverse of parse_iso8601_secs\n        let days_since_epoch = (one_hour_ago / 86400) as i64;\n        let secs_within_day = (one_hour_ago % 86400) as u32;\n\n        // Convert days since epoch to YYYY-MM-DD (inverse of ymd_to_days)\n        let (year, month, day) = days_to_ymd(days_since_epoch);\n\n        let hour = secs_within_day / 3600;\n        let min = (secs_within_day % 3600) / 60;\n        let sec = secs_within_day % 60;\n\n        format!(\"{:04}-{:02}-{:02}T{:02}:{:02}:{:02}Z\", year, month, day, hour, min, sec)\n    }\n\n    /// Convert days since epoch to (year, month, day)\n    ///\n    /// This is the inverse of ymd_to_days.         let seconds = ttfb.as_secs_f64();\n231\t            (bytes / seconds) / (1024.0 * 1024.0)\n232\t        } else {\n233\t            0.0\n234\t        };\n235\t\n236\t        Ok(ProbeInnerResult {\n237\t            connect_time,\n238\t            ttfb,\n239\t            throughput_mbs,\n240\t        })\n241\t    }\n242\t\n243\t    /// Calculate a combined score for provider selection\n244\t    ///\n245\t    /// Lower is better. Formula: connect_ms + ttfb_ms + (1 / throughput_mbs)\n246\t    fn calculate_score(result: &ProbeInnerResult) -> f64 {\n247\t        let connect_penalty = result.connect_time.as_millis() as f64;\n248\t        let ttfb_penalty = result.ttfb.as_millis() as f64;\n249\t        let throughput_penalty = if result.throughput_mbs > 0.0 {\n250\t            1000.0 / result.throughput_mbs\n251\t        } else {\n252\t            10000.0 // Large penalty for no throughput\n253\t        };\n254\t\n255\t        connect_penalty + ttfb_penalty + throughput_penalty\n256\t    }\n257\t\n258\t    /// Get the current git SHA for reproducibility\n259\t    fn get_git_sha() -> Option<String> {\n260\t        std::process::Command::new(\"git\")\n261\t            .args([\"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\"])\n262\t            .output()\n263\t            .ok()\n264\t            .and_then(|output| {\n265\t                let sha = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_string();\n266\t                if chrono::Utc::now();\n302\t                let age = now.signed_duration_since(timestamp);\n303\t                age.to_std().unwrap_or(Duration::ZERO) > max_age\n304\t            }\n305\t            Err(_) => true, // Invalid timestamp means stale\n306\t        }\n307\t    }\n308\t\n309\t    /// Record a failure for the given provider\n310\t    ///\n311\t    /// Increments the consecutive failure   /// This is a convenience method that combines the staleness check with the\n341\t    /// failure tracker check. Returns true if the probe results are fresh AND\n342\t    /// no tracked providers have exceeded the consecutive failure threshold.\n343\t    ///\n344\t    /// # Arguments\n345\t    /// * `results` - The probe results to check for staleness\n346\t    /// * `max_age` - Maximum age for probe results to be considered fresh\n347\t    ///\n348\t    /// # Example\n349\t    /// ```no_run\n350\t    /// use gribtract_fetch::probe::ProviderProbe;\n351\t    /// use std::time::Duration;\n352\t    ///\n353\t    /// let probe = ProviderProbe::new();\n354\t    /// let results = ProviderProbe::load_results(std::path::Path::new(\"provider-probe.json\")).unwrap();\n355\t    ///\n356\t    /// // Check if results are valid (fresh AND no providers need re-probing)\n357\t    /// if !probe.is_valid(&results, Duration::from_secs(24 * 3600)) {\n358\t    ///     // Trigger re-probe...\n359\t    /// }\n360\t    /// ```\n361\t    pub fn is_valid(&self, results: &ProviderProbeResults, max_age: Duration) -> bool {\n362\t        // First check staleness\n363\t        if Self::is_stale(results, max_age) {\n364\t            return false;\n365\t        }\n366\t\n367\t        // Then check if any tracked provider has exceeded the failure threshold\n368\t        // Use should_reprobe() for consistency\n369\t        for provider in self.consecutive_failures.keys() {\n370\t            if self.should_reprobe(provider) {\n371\t                return false;\n372\t            }\n373\t        }\n374\t\n375\t        true\n376\t    }\n377\t\n378\t    /// Get providers that need re-probing due to consecutive failures\n379\t    ///\n380\t    /// Returns a list of provider names that have exceeded the consecutive failure threshold.\n381\t    /// This can be used to log which providers are problematic before triggering a re-probe.\n382\t    ///\n383\t    /// #  Ok(result) => {\n                let _elapsed = start.elapsed();\n                ProbeResult {\n                    provider: provider.to_string(),\n                    probe_url: url.to_string(),\n (bytes / seconds) / (1024.0 * 1024.0)\n        } else {\n            0.0\n        };\n\n        Ok(ProbeInnerResult {\n            connect_time,\n            ttfb,\n            throughput_mbs,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Calculate a combined score for provider selection\n    ///\n    /// Lower is better. Err(_) => true, // Invalid timestamp means stale\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Record a failure for the given provider\n    ///\n    /// Increments the consecutive failure counter for the provider.\n    .get(provider)\n            .map(|&count| count >= self.consecutive_failure_threshold)\n            .unwrap_or(false)\n    }\n\n    /// Check if probe results are valid (fresh AND no providers need Returns true if the probe results are fresh AND\n    /// no tracked providers have exceeded the consecutive failure threshold.\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    /// * `results` - The probe results to check for staleness\n    /// * `max_age` - Maximum age for probe results to be considered fresh\n    ///\n    /// # Example\n    /// ```no_run\n    /// use gribtract_fetch::probe::ProviderProbe;\n    /// use std::time::Duration;\n    ///\n    /// let probe = ProviderProbe::new();\n    /// let results = ProviderProbe::load_results(std::path::Path::new(\"provider-probe.json\")).unwrap();\n    ///\n    /// // Check if results are valid (fresh AND no providers need re-probing)\n    /// if !probe.is_valid(&results, Duration::from_secs(24 * 3600)) {\n    ///     // Trigger re-probe...\n    /// }\n    /// ```\n    pub fn is_valid(&self, results: &ProviderProbeResults, max_age: Duration) -> bool {\n        // First check staleness\n        if Self::is_stale(results, max_age) {\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        // Then check if any tracked provider has exceeded the failure threshold\n        // Use should_reprobe() for consistency\n        for provider in self.consecutive_failures.keys() {\n            if self.should_reprobe(provider) {\n                return false;\n            }\n        }\n\n        true\n    }\n\n    /// Get providers that need re-probing due to consecutive failures\n    ///\n    /// Returns a list of provider names that have exceeded the consecutive failure threshold.\n    /// This can be used to log which providers are problematic before triggering a re-probe.\n    ///\n    /// # It should be used\n/// alongside the loaded provider-probe.json results.\n///\n/// # Example\n///\n/// This example shows how to use the failure tracker to monitor provider health:\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// use gribtract_fetch::probe::ProviderFailureTracker;\n///\n/// // Create a failure tracker with threshold of 3 consecutive errors\n/// let mut tracker = failures\");\n/// }\n///\n/// // Reset after successful request\n/// // tracker.record_success(\"s3:hrrr\");\n/// ```\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ProviderFailureTracker {\n    /// Consecutive the given provider\n    ///\n    /// Returns the current failure count after incrementing.\n    pub fn record_failure(&mut self, provider: &str) -> u32 {\n        let count =
